subject: Follow-up: prompt/output custody, residency & TTL for MedSys POC
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@medsys.health>; Michael Lin <michael.lin@medsys.health>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: prompt/output custody, residency & TTL for MedSys POC

Hi Emily / Michael,

Thanks for the call this morning — great to meet the MedSys team. As promised, quick recap of what we discussed re: PII and prompt/output handling for the POC and suggested next steps so your security and engineering teams have a concise reference.

High level (what Redwood does by default for hosted API):
- Prompt/response payloads: transient telemetry + logs used for debugging and quality are retained for 24 hours by default and then purged automatically.
- Model outputs: generation outputs are not used for model training and are only retained in logs for the same 24h window unless you enable longer retention.
- Access controls: logs are access-controlled, role-based, and encrypted at rest with platform KMS.

Options for POC (we covered three modes):
1) Hosted (fastest): 24h transient logs; we can add a retention SLA (e.g., 90 days) with an enterprise contract.
2) Dedicated (reserved capacity): you get tenant-level retention controls and can configure audit log retention; encryption and key access as part of the Dedicated contract.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem): we can disable persistent telemetry entirely — no outbound telemetry, customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), and logs kept only if you opt in.

Requested items from your team for the security checklist:
- Confirm whether you need: full transcript retention beyond 24h, or only aggregated metrics.
- Data residency preference (US - us-east/us-west or EU) for the POC environment.
- Any required encryption key posture (bring-your-own-key / Redwood-managed).

Attachments: I attached a short one-pager summarizing the modes and an initial MAAP workbook to capture retention TTLs — feel free to edit.

Next steps suggested:
- Security deep-dive with our security engineer (Lauren) next week to lock down retention + encryption.
- You update the MAAP workbook with desired TTLs and residency.

Thanks,

Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.ai]

Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt/output custody, residency & TTL for MedSys POC

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after reading the one-pager: 

1) For initial POC we want: prompts/outputs retained for 7 days only (us), then auto-delete. No long-term storage.
2) We want to understand what metadata remains in logs after content purging (e.g., request IDs, timestamps, anonymized model metrics).
3) Logging access: who at Redwood can access the raw prompts/outputs during the 7-day window? We need role-level names/roles (SRE, Support, Sales).
4) Residency: prefer us-west for now.

Also, can you confirm whether Private deployment is an option for the POC timeline (>8 weeks)? If not, we might request a very strict hosted contract for the 7-day TTL and proof of purging.

Emily
Emily Zhou
Director of AI Integrations, MedSys Health
emily.zhou@medsys.health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@medsys.health>, Michael Lin <michael.lin@medsys.health>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt/output custody, residency & TTL for MedSys POC

Emily — thanks, answered inline below and adding planned next actions.

1) TTL & auto-delete: we can support a 7-day TTL for the hosted POC environment. For the hosted API we will configure the workspace policy to auto-delete content after 7 days and provide proof of purge (audit logs) at the end of the POC window. Note: automated purge happens server-side; backups are included in purge workflow.

2) Metadata retained after purging: request IDs, timestamps, model variant, token counts, and anonymized latency/quality metrics are retained for 12 months by default for observability; these are not user-visible content and we can provide a redacted observability export. If you require only aggregated metrics (no per-request IDs) we can reduce retention of request-level IDs to 30 days.

3) Logging access: raw prompts/outputs are accessible only to the customer tenant (you) and platform SREs with approved escalation. For the POC we will:
   - Limit Redwood support access to 'redwood-support' role and require a JIRA ticket + approval for any manual access.
   - SREs (on-call) have ephemeral debug access (audited) and require manager approval for content viewing; all accesses are logged and visible to your security team on request.

4) Residency: we can spin up the POC in us-west; I'll note that in the MAAP.

Private deployment timeline: Private/VPC typically takes longer (4-8 weeks for packaging and network on-boarding). If your preferred timeline is under 8 weeks, Dedicated with strict retention policies is usually the fastest path to satisfy custody and TTL controls.

Attachments: I attached an updated MAAP workbook with suggested TTL cells filled for the 7-day option.

Planned next steps:
- Schedule security deep-dive with Lauren (I copied her) for Tue/Wed next week — can you confirm availability?
- We will produce a one-off purge demonstration at POC end and provide the purge audit.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik Iyer
